title: What is Bitcoin Keeper?
name: What is Bitcoin Keeper?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Bitcoin Keeper is a free, open-source bitcoin self-custody wallet on iOS and Android. It helps manage wallets, signing keys, backups, recovery and long-term access planning. It supports Single-Key and Multi-Key Wallets, including multisig. It is not an exchange or a custodial account. There are no subscriptions; donations are optional.

title: Is Bitcoin Keeper free? Are Pleb, Hodler and Diamond Hands subscriptions still required?
name: Is Bitcoin Keeper free? Are Pleb, Hodler and Diamond Hands subscriptions still required?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Bitcoin Keeper is free and has no subscription tiers. Pleb, Hodler and Diamond Hands pricing, paid upgrades and Restore Purchases instructions are obsolete. Wallet creation, signing, sending, receiving, backups, recovery, support and security are not gated by subscriptions or donations. Older articles describing tier limits must not be treated as current product information.

title: How can I support the developers or donate?
name: How can I support the developers or donate?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Donations are optional. Open More / Settings and choose Support the Developers. Donations help maintain Keeper. They do not unlock wallet, support, recovery or security features. Keeper is free, with no subscription tiers.

title: Can I buy, sell, swap or acquire bitcoin or USDT inside Keeper?
name: Can I buy, sell, swap or acquire bitcoin or USDT inside Keeper?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Buy, Sell, Swap and Acquire are removed from Bitcoin Keeper. Buy USDT via Ramp is also removed. Keeper is not an exchange or an on-ramp. Receiving, sending and managing bitcoin remain supported. USDT remains active as a separate wallet feature; removing the Buy USDT button did not remove USDT wallets.

title: What is Ask Keeper? Where did Zendesk, Knowledge Base and Keeper Learn go?
name: What is Ask Keeper? Where did Zendesk, Knowledge Base and Keeper Learn go?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Ask Keeper is the current question-and-answer help experience, replacing the retired Zendesk/ticketing knowledge base. On the website open Ask Keeper to ask questions or read Self-custody basics on the same page. Learn is combined into Ask Keeper; the old /learn route redirects there. The website and mobile app use the same Relay chat backend. Old Zendesk article links and Concierge ticket instructions are obsolete. Never put Recovery Keys, passcodes or private keys into a help conversation.

title: Does Keeper control my bitcoin? What does self-custody mean?
name: Does Keeper control my bitcoin? What does self-custody mean?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. You manage the keys needed to authorize spending and their backups. Keeper is not a custodial account. An optional Server Key can help sign as one key in a Multi-Key Wallet. Keeper cannot spend your bitcoin with that key alone. Self-custody requires maintaining the required signing keys and wallet configuration; it does not eliminate every trust or availability dependency.

title: Single-Key Wallet, hot wallet and Multi-Key Wallet: which setup should I choose?
name: Single-Key Wallet, hot wallet and Multi-Key Wallet: which setup should I choose?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. A Single-Key Wallet needs one key to spend and is simpler for everyday use. A hot wallet uses a signing key available on an online device. A Multi-Key Wallet needs multiple keys and can reduce dependence on one key, but requires more keys and backups to manage. A hardware key does not automatically make a wallet multisig. Choose a setup you can reliably back up and recover; do not assume that a more complex setup is automatically safer.

title: What is multisig? What do 2-of-3, 3-of-5 and custom m-of-n mean?
name: What is multisig? What do 2-of-3, 3-of-5 and custom m-of-n mean?
body: Reviewed 1 October 2026. A Multi-Key Wallet requires a threshold of keys to spend. In 2-of-3, 2 of the 3 keys are needed; in 3-of-5, 3 of the 5 are needed. The Recovery Key restores wallet configurations with a matching encrypted app backup. For independent recovery or use in another wallet, export a Wallet Configuration File. Keep access to enough separate signing keys; keys on one device or in one location can share a failure risk.

title: How do I get started, add a wallet or create a multisig wallet?
name: How do I get started, add a wallet or create a multisig wallet?
body: Reviewed 1 October 2026. Install Keeper from the official iOS or Android listing linked at bitcoinkeeper.app. Set the app passcode and back up the 12-word Recovery Key offline. Use Add Wallet from the home screen. Choose the wallet type, add the signing keys for a Multi-Key Wallet, and review the threshold. A Recovery Key restore with a matching encrypted app backup restores its wallet configurations. Exporting a Wallet Configuration File gives you an independent recovery option; signing keys outside the app need their own backups. Older Vault names, paid-tier steps and screenshots may be obsolete.

title: What is the Recovery Key? Are the 12 words a backup for every signer?
name: What is the Recovery Key? Are the 12 words a backup for every signer?
body: Reviewed 1 October 2026. The Recovery Key is Keeper’s 12-word backup for restoring the complete app state from a matching encrypted app backup, including wallets, wallet configurations, signers, labels and saved node settings. Keep it offline and never share it. Hardware signing keys live outside the app; recovering Keeper does not recreate their private keys or bypass a Multi-Key Wallet’s signing threshold. An exported Wallet Configuration File is an independent fallback or interoperability tool, not a routine prerequisite for restoring the app.

title: How should I back up Keeper? Why confirm the Recovery Key?
name: How should I back up Keeper? Why confirm the Recovery Key?
body: Reviewed 1 October 2026. Back up the primary 12-word Recovery Key offline and confirm it to check that you recorded it correctly. With a matching encrypted app backup, the Recovery Key restores Keeper and its wallet configurations. You can also export a Wallet Configuration File for independent recovery or use in compatible software. Preserve separate hardware or imported signing-key backups according to their device instructions. Cloud Backup and Assisted Server Backup do not replace the Recovery Key. Never put its words in chat, email, online notes or support tickets.

title: I forgot my passcode or lost my phone. How do I recover Keeper?
name: I forgot my passcode or lost my phone. How do I recover Keeper?
body: Reviewed 1 October 2026. The passcode unlocks the local app; it does not replace the Recovery Key. Use the existing-app recovery flow and your 12-word Recovery Key. When a matching encrypted app backup is available, Keeper restores the app state, including wallets, wallet configurations, signers, labels and saved node settings. If no matching app backup exists, the Recovery Key alone recreates only its default derived wallet; separate configuration exports may then help recover other wallets. Hardware signing keys remain outside the app, and their own backups are still needed to meet a Multi-Key Wallet’s spending threshold.

title: What is Personal Cloud Backup? Does it save the Recovery Key or private keys?
name: What is Personal Cloud Backup? Does it save the Recovery Key or private keys?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Personal Cloud Backup / Cloud Backup saves wallet configuration material to help recreate wallet setups. It does not replace your offline Recovery Key or independent signing-device backups. A Wallet Configuration File contains no private keys. Do not assume you are fully backed up just because cloud backup completed.

title: What is Assisted Server Backup? Is it the same as Server Key?
name: What is Assisted Server Backup? Is it the same as Server Key?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Assisted Server Backup backs up encrypted data using a community-run Keeper server. Its entry is More → Backup and Recovery. It is distinct from Personal Cloud Backup and from Server Key, which is a signing key. Assisted Server Backup does not replace the offline 12-word Recovery Key and does not give Keeper authority to spend your bitcoin.

title: What is a Wallet Configuration File, BSMS or descriptor?
name: What is a Wallet Configuration File, BSMS or descriptor?
body: Reviewed 1 October 2026. A Wallet Configuration File describes a wallet’s public keys and spending structure; it contains no private keys. Keeper normally restores wallet configurations with the app when a matching encrypted app backup is available. Export the file as an independent fallback or to recreate the wallet in compatible software. Recreating the configuration does not authorize spending: the required signing keys are still needed. Treat the file as private financial information because public wallet data can reveal balances and activity.

title: What does importing a wallet mean? Can I recreate a Keeper wallet in another app?
name: What does importing a wallet mean? Can I recreate a Keeper wallet in another app?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Importing wallet configuration recreates a specific wallet in Keeper or other compatible software. It does not move bitcoin and does not necessarily restore the whole Keeper app. Use compatible Wallet Configuration Files / descriptors and the required signing keys. Compatibility depends on the wallet format, network and script features supported by the destination app; do not assume every wallet supports advanced timelock or inheritance rules.

title: What is a watch-only wallet or external xpub?
name: What is a watch-only wallet or external xpub?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. A watch-only wallet uses public information to view addresses, balances and transactions. An extended public key (xpub) helps derive public addresses; it cannot sign spending transactions. Watch-only access is not a recovery substitute for private signing keys. Sharing an xpub can reveal financial activity, so do not post it publicly. Confirm the correct wallet type, derivation and network when importing.

title: What is a signing device, Mobile Key or Seed Key?
name: What is a signing device, Mobile Key or Seed Key?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. A signing device holds or controls a signing key. Keeper can combine hardware or software signers in a Multi-Key Wallet. Mobile Key is a key managed using a mobile device; Seed Key imports existing seed material. These are different from Keeper’s primary Recovery Key backup. Reusing a key across wallets creates a shared dependency. Never submit a seed or private key to Ask Keeper; enter secret material only in the intended trusted recovery/import flow.

title: Which hardware wallets can I use with Keeper?
name: Which hardware wallets can I use with Keeper?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Keeper supports hardware and software signing devices on iOS and Android. Supported signer families include COLDCARD, Passport, TAPSIGNER, Blockstream Jade, SeedSigner, Keystone, BitBox02, Ledger, Trezor and Specter DIY. Connection methods depend on device, phone and firmware: QR, NFC, SD card or a web bridge may be involved. Use the supported-device picker and current device instructions. Do not assume every device supports every advanced wallet script or transport.

title: What should I check before signing or updating hardware firmware?
name: What should I check before signing or updating hardware firmware?
body: Reviewed 1 October 2026. Review the recipient address, amount, fee and source wallet. Use signing hardware that can independently verify the wallet policy and recognize change where supported. Before updating firmware, preserve signer backups and Wallet Configuration Files and follow official device guidance; never enter a seed into an update website. COLDCARD users should check Coinkite’s current security advisory at https://blog.coinkite.com/coldcard-mk3-seed-generation-warning/ . Updating affected firmware does not repair a seed generated on it; follow the vendor’s migration guidance. Check current advisories for your exact device model.

title: What is the Server Key? Can Keeper spend with it alone?
name: What is the Server Key? Can Keeper spend with it alone?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Server Key is an optional Keeper-assisted signing key in a Multi-Key Wallet. It is independently generated, not derived from your Recovery Key, and stored server-side. It is not your only signer: Keeper cannot spend your bitcoin with Server Key alone. It can simplify some signing flows and may use policies or 2FA. Review the actual app policy, waiting period and other required keys; do not assume a universal spend cap or delay.

title: What are Assisted Keys?
name: What are Assisted Keys?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Assisted Keys is a grouping for Keeper-supported keys such as Server Key, Inheritance Key and Emergency Key. Each has a different purpose and wallet rules. They are not interchangeable and are not a replacement for Recovery Key or wallet configuration backups. Review which keys are needed for ordinary spending and which delayed access paths exist.

title: What is a Collaborative Wallet? Is it different from Multi User Mode?
name: What is a Collaborative Wallet? Is it different from Multi User Mode?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Collaborative Wallet is a fixed 2-of-3 shared-control wallet. It is intended for shared responsibility across people or roles, rather than a generic custom threshold builder. Multi User Mode provides isolated app profiles on one device and is a different feature. Sharing control of keys does not by itself establish shared legal ownership.

title: What is an Inheritance Key? How do heirs get access?
name: What is an Inheritance Key? How do heirs get access?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Inheritance Key provides a delayed access path for an heir or trusted party under the wallet rules. It is not a daily spending key and may increase total keys without reducing today’s normal spending threshold. Plan required keys, configuration files, trusted contacts and instructions. The access conditions are part of the wallet script; changing them may require a new wallet and moving bitcoin. Key access does not transfer legal ownership.

title: Can I reset an Inheritance Key or change a wallet timelock?
name: Can I reset an Inheritance Key or change a wallet timelock?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Wallet script conditions are fixed when created. Resetting an Inheritance Key, changing delayed access rules or changing a Wallet Timelock may require a rollover to a new wallet and transfer of funds. Follow the app’s actual migration flow, preserve old configurations and signing keys, and review the new threshold and delay before confirming. Do not treat script changes like editing a password.

title: What is an Emergency Key? How is it different from Inheritance Key?
name: What is an Emergency Key? How is it different from Inheritance Key?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Emergency Key is a separate advanced option for delayed recovery access when normal access is unavailable. Inheritance Key is a delayed access path intended for heirs or trusted parties. Review who holds each key, when it can be used and how it changes the wallet rules. Never describe Emergency Key as the same feature or key as Inheritance Key.

title: What is Wallet Timelock? Can I spend before it ends?
name: What is Wallet Timelock? Can I spend before it ends?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Wallet Timelock prevents spending until the selected time condition is satisfied. It cannot be bypassed through app support, a passcode reset or an ordinary settings change. Understand the exact date and access conditions before creating the wallet. Changing script rules may need a new wallet and moving funds; do not promise that locked funds can be moved early.

title: How should I plan inheritance and access if Keeper is unavailable?
name: How should I plan inheritance and access if Keeper is unavailable?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Preserve interoperable wallet configurations, sufficient signing keys and clear offline instructions for trusted people. Inheritance tools and letters help explain where information is stored and who can access it, but do not establish legal ownership or guarantee that heirs can spend without the required keys and script conditions. Plan compatible recovery software and relevant documentation; do not place actual seed words in a letter shared online.

title: What happens after changing a key, signer or wallet scheme?
name: What happens after changing a key, signer or wallet scheme?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Changing the underlying key or spending scheme can require a new wallet configuration and moving bitcoin. Replacing a signing device with another holding the same key is conceptually different from rotating to a new key. Preserve backups and verify the resulting public key and wallet policy. Keeper automatically retains the previous configuration as an Archived Wallet after scheme/key changes. Old receive addresses still belong to the old configuration.

title: What is an Archived Wallet? Can I spend from it?
name: What is an Archived Wallet? Can I spend from it?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. An Archived Wallet is an older configuration automatically retained after scheme/key changes. It is not permanently read-only and not a normal manual archive action. To use it, unarchive it first. Funds sent to old addresses belong to that old configuration; spending requires its old signing-key quorum. Do not discard old keys/configurations until old funds and future old-address receipts are accounted for.

title: Hidden Wallet, Hidden Key and Archived Wallet: what is the difference?
name: Hidden Wallet, Hidden Key and Archived Wallet: what is the difference?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Hidden Wallet is a reversible visibility setting: it removes the wallet from the normal home view without changing its underlying spending rules. Hidden Key is a separate key visibility feature. Archived Wallet is an older configuration retained after scheme/key changes and must be unarchived before use. Hiding is not deleting, archiving or a guarantee of protection under coercion.

title: What is a Canary Wallet?
name: What is a Canary Wallet?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Canary Wallet uses a small amount of bitcoin as an early warning signal associated with signing-key compromise. Unexpected movement can indicate a security problem worth investigating. It does not prevent compromise or guarantee detection. If alerted, examine the affected keys and other wallets that depend on them before taking an irreversible action.

title: What is Multi User Mode?
name: What is Multi User Mode?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Multi User Mode provides separate profiles within one Keeper app, each with its own PIN and isolated data. The PIN determines which profile opens. Backups and recovery are profile-specific. It is distinct from a Collaborative Wallet: profiles on a shared device do not create a 2-of-3 shared-control wallet.

title: How do I switch between Mainnet and Testnet?
name: How do I switch between Mainnet and Testnet?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Network Type is a global app setting at More → App Settings → Network Type. Mainnet and Testnet have separate wallets, keys and nodes. Testnet coins are for testing and have no mainnet value. This setting is not inside an individual signer’s settings. Feature availability varies by network; use the current app’s supported choices and do not assume advanced assisted keys or USDT are available on Testnet.

title: How do I receive bitcoin?
name: How do I receive bitcoin?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Open the intended bitcoin wallet and its Receive flow. Check the wallet and network, copy or scan the address and verify it before sharing. Where supported, verify the address with an independently verifying signing device. Receiving does not require spending signatures. Old addresses after key/scheme changes belong to the older Archived Wallet configuration; preserve its keys. Use a small test amount when validating a new setup.

title: How do I send bitcoin or collect multisig signatures?
name: How do I send bitcoin or collect multisig signatures?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Open the intended wallet’s Send flow, enter the destination and amount, and review the recipient, amount, fee and wallet. For a Multi-Key Wallet, collect the required threshold of signatures from available signing keys. A PSBT carries a partially signed bitcoin transaction between signers; it is not a seed or Recovery Key. Broadcast only after reviewing and completing the required signatures. Bitcoin transactions cannot ordinarily be reversed after confirmation.

title: Why is my transaction pending or unconfirmed?
name: Why is my transaction pending or unconfirmed?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Unconfirmed bitcoin transactions are included in wallet balance and shown as pending/unconfirmed in history. Displayed balance is not the same as final confirmation. Confirmation time depends on network conditions and fees. Review the transaction’s status and supported fee-management options in the current app. Do not promise a fixed confirmation time or initiate a duplicate transfer simply because it is pending.

title: How should I use labels, UTXO coin control and Do Not Spend?
name: How should I use labels, UTXO coin control and Do Not Spend?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Labels help record transaction and coin context. UTXO coin control lets you manage the specific bitcoin coins used in a spend; Do Not Spend can exclude selected coins from normal selection. Keep privacy and fee effects in mind when combining coins. Do not treat a label or a coin-selection suggestion as a guarantee against tracking. Check the installed app’s current controls before changing coin status.

title: What are signer health checks?
name: What are signer health checks?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. A health check helps confirm that a signing device remains accessible and can participate in your wallet. Manual Health Check is supported. A successful check does not replace offline signer backups, wallet configuration backups or a tested recovery plan. Check enough distinct keys to meet your spending threshold and account for keys reused across wallets.

title: Can I use my own node, Tor or Orbot?
name: Can I use my own node, Tor or Orbot?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Keeper offers own-node and Tor/Orbot connectivity options. Use the current app’s node settings and the correct global Network Type. Tor can help protect connection privacy but does not guarantee anonymity or protect a compromised device. Verify node availability and connection settings if balances or transactions do not sync. Never share a node credential in Ask Keeper.

title: What data or biometrics does Keeper collect?
name: What data or biometrics does Keeper collect?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Diagnostics are permission-based and should exclude Recovery Keys, passcodes and private keys. Biometrics are handled through the operating system; Keeper does not collect your raw biometric template. Self-custody is not a promise that every service sees no metadata. Consult the current Privacy Policy for exact collection and service details. Never disclose secret key material to support.

title: Where are the current Privacy Policy and Terms of Service?
name: Where are the current Privacy Policy and Terms of Service?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Read the current official Privacy Policy at https://www.bitcoinkeeper.app/privacy-policy and Terms of Service at https://www.bitcoinkeeper.app/terms-of-service. Retired Zendesk legal article copies are not the current destination. Ask Keeper can explain product behavior but cannot replace the actual published legal documents.

title: Does Keeper still support USDT? Which network?
name: Does Keeper still support USDT? Which network?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Yes. USDT remains active as a separate USDT Wallet feature on the mobile app. It uses USDT TRC-20 on Tron and is available for the supported mainnet setup. Buy USDT via Ramp is removed. USDT does not use bitcoin multisig, UTXOs or bitcoin inheritance rules. Never send ERC-20 USDT, bitcoin or an unsupported token to its USDT receive address.

title: How do I receive USDT? Which address should I use?
name: How do I receive USDT? Which address should I use?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Open the USDT Wallet and choose Receive. Use the GasFree receive address displayed by that wallet, not an assumed ordinary Tron address from another app. Send only USDT TRC-20 on Tron. Check the receiving address and network carefully before sending; unsupported tokens or networks may cause loss or inaccessible funds. A bitcoin receiving address is unrelated.

title: Does gas-free USDT mean no fees or no TRX?
name: Does gas-free USDT mean no fees or no TRX?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Keeper uses GasFree permit transfers for supported USDT Wallets, so the user does not need to hold TRX for these transfers. Gas-free does not mean free of charge: a transfer fee and, for a new account, an activation fee can apply. Review the current fee breakdown and total USDT outflow on the confirmation screen; do not rely on a fixed historical fee.

title: How do I send USDT or use Send Max?
name: How do I send USDT or use Send Max?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Open the intended USDT Wallet, choose Send, enter a valid Tron destination and amount, then review the destination, transfer fee, any account activation fee and total outflow. Send Max deducts applicable fees. Keeper submits a GasFree permit transfer when you confirm. Wait for an existing pending transfer or activation where warned. Frozen amounts in pending transfers reduce the available balance.

title: Can I import an existing USDT wallet? Are all Tron balances automatically imported?
name: Can I import an existing USDT wallet? Are all Tron balances automatically imported?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. The current app can import a USDT Wallet using its BIP-39 mnemonic, separately from wallets derived from Keeper’s primary Recovery Key. The import creates the corresponding Tron account and initializes its GasFree account. Do not promise that every external wallet, derivation path or ordinary Tron account balance appears at the GasFree receive address. Verify address and balance compatibility before sending. Never enter the mnemonic into Ask Keeper or a website chat.

title: How do I back up or recover a USDT wallet?
name: How do I back up or recover a USDT wallet?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. New USDT Wallets created by Keeper derive a child mnemonic from the app’s primary Recovery Key using BIP-85. Imported USDT Wallets use their own imported mnemonic and are separate; preserve that backup independently. Keep the primary 12-word Recovery Key offline and retain wallet recovery information. USDT Wallet settings provide authenticated Wallet Recovery Key export where supported. Never assume the primary Recovery Key alone regenerates every externally imported wallet.

title: Why is my USDT transaction missing, confirming or failed?
name: Why is my USDT transaction missing, confirming or failed?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Check that the transfer used USDT TRC-20 on Tron and the wallet’s displayed GasFree receive address. Confirming is pending; a trace identifier may exist before the final transaction hash. Completed transfers link to a Tron explorer. Failed transfers need their actual failure reviewed; do not repeat a payment blindly. Available balance excludes amounts frozen for pending transfers. Network mismatch and an ordinary address vs GasFree address can explain a missing balance.

title: Is my USDT wallet the same security model as a bitcoin multisig wallet?
name: Is my USDT wallet the same security model as a bitcoin multisig wallet?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. No. USDT Wallet is a separate Tron/GasFree feature using its wallet key; bitcoin multisig, UTXO management and signing-device health checks do not automatically apply. Do not claim that the USDT Wallet inherits a bitcoin Multi-Key Wallet’s threshold protection or that hardware multisig protects its balance. Preserve its correct recovery material and review stablecoin/service dependencies.

title: Does Keeper require KYC or an exchange account?
name: Does Keeper require KYC or an exchange account?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Creating and using a bitcoin self-custody wallet in Keeper does not require an exchange account or identity verification. Keeper is free and has no subscription tiers. Removed Buy/Sell/Swap or Ramp flows should not be described as current. Service metadata and diagnostics are separate from KYC; read the current Privacy Policy for collection details.

title: Do hidden wallets guarantee protection under coercion?
name: Do hidden wallets guarantee protection under coercion?
body: Reviewed 30 September 2026. Hidden Wallets and Hidden Keys reduce normal visibility and are managed through Settings / More → Manage Wallets or Manage Keys. They do not guarantee safety under physical coercion or prevent a determined person discovering wallet information. Hiding is a visibility action, distinct from Archived Wallets and spending policy. Plan physical safety and backups separately; never split and distribute Recovery Key words casually as an inheritance shortcut.
